title: Rate limits / org & project keys demo with Verdant Clinic
summary: Redwood AE and SE demoed org-level and project-level rate limiting, API keys model, quotas, and multi-tenant controls. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated; primary concerns were per-project isolation, burst behavior, audit logs, and SSO provisioning of keys. Agreed next steps: share pricing sheet, security docs, and setup a 2-week pilot org with sample project keys + test quotas/benchmarks.
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-25 16:00 PDT | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Diaz (Redwood SE), Jason Patel (Verdant CTO), Priya Rao (Verdant Dir Eng), Tom Greene (Verdant DevOps), Emily Carter (Verdant Security), Aisha Khan (Verdant PM)

Summary: quick walkthrough of org/project key controls and rate limiting in the console + API demo.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, i'll hand it over to Carlos to jump into the demo but real quick i'm maya your AE from Redwood, we scheduled 40 minutes so we'll go through org keys, project quotas, and then leave time for q and a.
00:12 Carlos: cool thanks maya. so i'll share my screen, let me know if you can't see. (pause) ok see a console screen - apologies sometimes our staging org name renders as redwood-stg, it's our demo tenant.
00:28 Jason: yep seeing it.
00:30 Carlos: great. so first concept - org level limits vs project level. think of org as the top container for billing, SSO provisioning, audit logs. projects are where you create API keys that map to a single service or app. you can set quotas at either layer, and keys inherit policies from both - more specific wins.
01:05 Priya: quick question, for our use case we have multi-tenant apps per clinic location, would each location be a project?
01:15 Carlos: you could do that, yes. many customers create a project per environment or per tenant. you can also do per-route enforcement via the API key metadata if you want more granular controls.
01:28 Tom: how do bursts work - like pulse traffic at 2pm daily for notifications? we worry about throttles causing failed jobs.
01:36 Carlos: good question. we support two levers: steady-state quotas (tokens/minute) and a burst buffer. burst allows short-term exceedance up to a configured burst_limit and is consumed from a burst bucket that refills over time. when burst is exhausted, calls receive 429 with Retry-After header. you can also configure automatic fallbacks to lower-cost model variants on throttle.
01:58 Emily: on 429 responses, do we get headers for remaining quota? we need them for client-side backoff and alerting.
02:06 Carlos: yes - X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset and Retry-After are included. sometimes our CDN layer may alter exact header names in edge cases but that's the general pattern.
02:20 Maya: i'll show the console policy page now - this is where you create org policies and project overrides.
02:30 Carlos: (navigating) here is an example policy: org default: 10k tokens/min, burst 50k, per-project overrides: project-a -> 2k tokens/min. you can also attach tags for billing.
02:45 Priya: do these quotas apply to embeddings and generation separately or is it token-agnostic?
02:52 Carlos: currently token-based quota covers generation calls; embeddings are metered as embedding units and can have separate quotas. you can set both on the policy.
03:06 Jason: what about per-key billing and metering? we want each clinic to get a monthly invoice slice.
03:12 Maya: our billing API and CSV usage exports support project-level usage breakdown. you can either bill back by project IDs or map projects to internal billing codes.
03:24 Carlos: i'll flip to the API demo - hitting the /v1/generate endpoint with project key header x-redwood-key: proj_live_abc123. you'll see response headers with quota info and a billing tag.
03:38 (keyboard sounds)
03:44 Carlos: ok request sent... the response comes back with streaming tokens, and headers: X-RateLimit-Limit:2000, X-RateLimit-Remaining:1996, X-RateLimit-Reset:164, Billing-Project: clinic-west. this is the typical flow.
04:05 Tom: if a key is compromised how fast can we rotate keys? and do old tokens immediately invalidate?
04:12 Carlos: you can rotate via the console or API. creating a new key doesn't automatically revoke the old one, you must explicitly revoke, but we do have a key rotation endpoint that can create new key and set the old key to revoked in one call. revocation is immediate and will be reflected at the edge within seconds typically.
04:29 Emily: audit logs? we need full traceability for SOC2.
04:34 Maya: audit logs are available at org level with event types: key_create, key_revoke, policy_change, login. logs are exportable to S3 and forwardable to Splunk/Datadog. retention tiers are configurable - enterprise plan includes 12 months by default.
04:50 Priya: any RBAC, can we restrict who can create project keys?
04:56 Carlos: yes RBAC maps to roles: Org Admin, Project Admin, Developer, Read-only. you can enable SSO + SCIM to sync groups and assign roles.
05:10 Aisha: what's the difference between Dedicated and Hosted for these controls? we may need dedicated for data isolation.
05:17 Maya: control plane features are consistent across Hosted and Dedicated. Dedicated gives you isolated inference clusters and data plane isolation - logs and telemetry can be kept in your VPC. some advanced network controls (private peering, on-prem connectors) are Dedicated-only.
05:34 Jason: latency counts - any throttles due to rate limiting happen at the edge, do you have a per-tenant queue?
05:41 Carlos: we try to fail fast. throttles return 429. for queued burst smoothing, we have an optional request queue for Dedicated customers that can smooth spikes but adds small queuing latency. for most Hosted customers we recommend burst buffers rather than queues.
05:58 Emily: what about test mode and test keys? we want to run load tests without impacting production quotas.
06:05 Carlos: we provide sandbox orgs and test keys that are token-limited and not billed. they'll mimic the quota behavior but you can supply a higher burst for testing. we also support a 'dry-run' header so policies log but don't enforce.
06:20 Priya: can policies be applied via infrastructure as code? we run Terraform for infra governance.
06:26 Carlos: yes we have a Terraform provider and an API for all policy objects - you can manage org policies, project creations, keys, and RBAC via IaC.
06:33 Jason: curious about soft limits vs hard limits - can we set alerts before hitting limit?
06:38 Carlos: absolutely - you can create alerting rules tied to percent thresholds and send to Slack/email/webhook. we also emit metrics to Prometheus/Datadog.
06:47 Maya: i'll demo creating a project key and applying an override: (click) create project -> clinic-east -> generate key -> set quota to 5k tokens/min, burst 20k.
07:05 Carlos: now i'll simulate a traffic spike using a small script, sending bursts until we hit the threshold, you'll see the headers change and then a 429 with Retry-After when exhausted.
07:20 (script runs)
07:28 Priya: i'm seeing the 429 in the console logs. headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining:0, Retry-After: 30.
07:37 Tom: ok that's good. how does automatic fallback work? could we automatically route to a cheaper model if quota exceeded instead of failing?
07:45 Carlos: yes, you can configure an overflow policy per project: fallback model id or fallback org tier. fallback is supported if the models are compatible; we do warn about potential quality deltas. fallback is performed at the routing layer so it's near-zero latency overhead.
07:59 Aisha: any limits on number of projects per org? we could have hundreds.
08:04 Carlos: current soft limit is 2,000 projects per org; we can raise that for enterprise accounts.
08:12 Emily: how about API key scoping to routes and IP allowlist?
08:17 Carlos: key metadata supports allowed_routes and ip_allowlist arrays. note IP allowlist works for non-browsers; for browser embedded clients we recommend short-lived keys via our session token exchange.
08:29 Jason: ok let's talk POC. we want a 2-week pilot with per-clinic projects for 5 clinics, simulate daily burst profile and validate billing exports plus logs.
08:40 Maya: sounds reasonable. we'll provision a trial org, create 5 projects, and give you test keys you can swap to prod keys later.
08:48 Priya: who will own the setup? can you provide a runbook?
08:52 Maya: yes i'll send a runbook and a checklist. Carlos will help with the initial project creation and Terraform snippets.
09:00 Carlos: quick note on error semantics: if a project's quota is exceeded we return 429 with code quota_exceeded; if org is over total quota we return 429 with code org_quota_exceeded. This lets clients distinguish transient project throttles from org-level limits.
09:16 Tom: do you expose per-request tracing ids? we want to tie logs back to our request ids.
09:21 Carlos: every request has a request_id header plus we can inject trace context. logs include the request id and the project_id, key_id, and route.
09:30 Emily: for compliance, do you provide signed audit logs or tamper-evident logs?
09:35 Maya: we support log signing for enterprise packages and can store logs in write-once buckets; also HSM-backed keys for signing available on request.
09:45 Priya: any gotchas around key rotation for live clients? we have mobile apps that cache keys.
09:52 Carlos: recommend short-lived keys for mobile and a server-side token exchange. for server to server you can rotate nightly and have a grace period flag to accept old keys for N minutes during rotation.
10:04 Aisha: I saw a doc link in chat about rate limit headers, can you drop the link?
10:09 Maya: sure i'll include links after the call - security whitepaper, rate-limits API doc, and a pricing CSV sample.
10:15 (Q&A continues covering minor details and edge cases)
10:44 Maya: ok wrapping up - recap: Redwood to provision a trial org, create 5 project keys, provide Terraform snippets, runbook, pricing, and security docs. Verdant will run burst tests and share results; we'll schedule a follow-up at the end of pilot to review billing/observability.
10:58 Jason: sounds good, thanks everyone.
11:02 Maya: thanks all.

Notes: transcription imperfect in places; some proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., header names, model ids). references: /docs/rate-limits, /docs/api-keys, pricing-sheet.csv, security-whitepaper.pdf
